 What Magnachip Semiconductor (MX) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
 Magnachip Semiconductor logo MarketBeat Sun, November 8, 2026 at 12:14 AM EST 6 min read MX +17.07% 
 KRW=X +0.51% 
 Key Points 
 Interested in Magnachip Semiconductor Corp.? Here are five stocks we like better. 
 Q3 results were pressured by currency and supply constraints: Revenue fell 4.3% year over year to $44 million, while gross margin dropped to 14%, below guidance of 17%–19%, largely because the Korean won strengthened and packaging bottlenecks limited shipments. 
 Magnachip expects margins to fall further before recovering: Q4 revenue is forecast at $41 million–$45 million and gross margin at 10%–12%, reflecting seasonal softness, the Gumi fab shutdown for a substation upgrade, and currency pressure. The company expects Q4 to be the margin low point as fab operations normalize. 
 The company is pursuing higher-value products and a Navitas partnership: Magnachip aims to move beyond price-driven products toward differentiated solutions for applications such as AI servers and industrial equipment, with initial sampling targeted within 12 months. First-generation silicon carbide and silicon products developed with Navitas are expected to enter sampling in H2 2027. 
 5 Semiconductor stocks under $10 
 Magnachip Semiconductor (NYSE:MX) reported lower third-quarter revenue and a gross margin below its forecast as a stronger Korean won and packaging constraints weighed on results. The company also projected a further margin decline in the fourth quarter, while outlining plans to shift toward more differentiated power semiconductor products. 
 Revenue from continuing operations fell 4.3% year over year to $44 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, within the company's forecast range of $41.5 million to $45.5 million. Revenue declined 1.6% from the second quarter.

 Chief Financial Officer Shinyoung Park attributed the decline primarily to lower customer volumes in some consumer applications and packaging constraints that temporarily limited Magnachip's ability to meet growing demand in certain product areas. The company is addressing the bottlenecks and expects some benefits in coming quarters, Park said. 
 Currency Pressure Weighs on Margins 
 Gross profit margin from continuing operations fell to 14%, below Magnachip's guidance range of 17% to 19%. That compared with 18.6% a year earlier and 19.3% in the second quarter.

 SGH Bottomed, But Can It Reverse And Move Higher? 
 Park said the principal reason for the shortfall against guidance was a sharper-than-expected appreciation of the Korean won against the U.S. dollar. A substantial portion of Magnachip's costs are denominated in won, while much of its revenue is in dollars. 
 Story Continues Adjusted operating loss widened to $8.6 million from $7.4 million a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $3.5 million from negative $4 million. Non-GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.29, compared with $0.01 a year earlier. 
 → Google's Credit Backstop May Be TeraWulf's Biggest Advantage 
 Park said the larger per-share loss was primarily attributable to a non-cash income tax expense from a reduction in deferred tax assets following a Korean tax audit involving differences in the interpretation of tax law. 
 Magnachip ended the quarter with $86.9 million in cash, down $1 million from the end of the second quarter. Cash outflows, including $2.3 million in capital expenditures, were partially offset by a $5 million strategic equity investment from Navitas Semiconductor and other cash movements. Total borrowings were $47.1 million at quarter-end. 
 Fourth-Quarter Outlook 
 For the fourth quarter, Magnachip forecast revenue from continuing operations of $41 million to $45 million, citing typical seasonal softness. The midpoint of $43 million would represent a 2.2% sequential decline and a 6% increase from the fourth quarter of 2025. 
 The company expects gross margin of 10% to 12%, down from 14% in the third quarter. Park attributed the expected decline primarily to lower utilization associated with a previously announced shutdown of the Gumi fabrication plant for a substation upgrade, as well as the impact of the won's appreciation. 
 Park said Magnachip expects the fourth quarter to mark the low point for gross margin, with a return to normal fab operations gradually easing manufacturing cost pressures. The company is also considering selective price increases to offset recent supply-chain cost increases, she said. 
 Product Roadmap and Navitas Partnership 
 Chief Executive Officer Chae Lee said Magnachip is working to move away from competing primarily on price with traditional second-source products. The company has announced 57 new-generation products so far in 2026 and expects approximately 85 by year-end, up from 55 in the prior year. 
 Lee said most of the recent introductions remain traditional products with limited differentiation. The next priority is to develop higher-value solutions incorporating intelligence, sensing and monitoring capabilities for applications including AI servers, industrial equipment and consumer products. Magnachip is targeting initial sampling of those products within 12 months. 
 Its longer-term roadmap combines Navitas' high-voltage silicon carbide technology with Magnachip's silicon technology and manufacturing capabilities. Lee said joint development of the first generation began a few months ago, with sampling expected in the second half of 2027. The partnership also includes resale of a Navitas product and plans to bring Navitas technology into Magnachip's Gumi fab. 
 During the question-and-answer session, Lee said the company's existing second-source and discrete-product strategy was unlikely to produce strong revenue or profit growth. He said the planned module solutions could command higher average selling prices by providing customers with benefits such as greater efficiency and reliability. 
 Asked about his open-market share purchases in September, Lee said he believed Magnachip was undervalued relative to its intrinsic and long-term potential value, and expressed confidence in the company's people, technology and product roadmap. 
 About Magnachip Semiconductor (NYSE:MX) 
 Magnachip Semiconductor Corporation (NYSE: MX) is a semiconductor company that designs and supplies analog and mixed-signal products. Its portfolio is focused primarily on power semiconductors and display solutions used in consumer electronics, communications equipment, automotive applications, industrial systems and other electronic devices. 
 The company's power products include metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs), insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs), power integrated circuits and other discrete semiconductor devices designed to manage power conversion, distribution and efficiency.
